intended_object: The sub-simplicial set S^U(X) of the singular simplicial set Sing(X), made of the 𝒰-small singular simplices: maps σ : Δⁿ → X whose image lies in some member U_i of a family 𝒰 = (U_i) of open sets. Its chains are the 𝒰-small singular chains C^𝒰_*(X) used in the excision / small-simplices theorem. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module name (SmallChains).
explanation: At level n the definition takes the set of singular n-simplices x whose underlying continuous map Δⁿ → X (`X.toSSetObjEquiv n x`) has range contained in some `U i`. Closure under the simplicial operators holds because the range of σ ∘ Δ(f) is contained in the range of σ, and the proof shows exactly this. So this is the standard 𝒰-small singular subcomplex. The definition does not require 𝒰 to cover X, which is correct: the covering (or interiors-covering) condition belongs to the small-simplices theorem, not to the definition. Hatcher states the notion for an arbitrary family of subsets, while this definition uses `Opens X`. That is a small restriction and matches how the notion is almost always used (open covers for excision and Mayer–Vietoris), so it is not a real narrowing. Mathlib has the singular simplicial set `TopCat.toSSet` but no counterpart for small simplices.
